title: Cycloidal drive: output coupler (PETG-CF)
prompt:
Component analysis: the output coupler of an open-source, 3D-printable 15:1 cycloidal gearbox. part.step holds the single solid in millimetres (33 faces, volume 2063 mm^3). faces.json lists every face with its index, type, area, centroid and normal/axis; use the geometry, not a CAD system's own face numbering.

Material: PETG-CF, linear isotropic elastic, E = 3000 MPa, Poisson ratio 0.36.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements, no gravity, no contact.
Supports: all three displacement components are zero on face 5: cylinder, area 33.52 mm^2, centroid (76.619, -0.908, 22.737) mm, radius 2.5 mm, axis (1.0, 0.0, -0.0) through (79.025, -0.0, 20.5) (hole/bore surface); face 6: cylinder, area 117.81 mm^2, centroid (76.525, 1.588, 20.397) mm, radius 2.5 mm, axis (1.0, 0.0, -0.0) through (79.025, -0.0, 20.5) (hole/bore surface).
Load: total force (100.052, 0.000, 0.000) N applied as a uniform surface traction (constant force per unit area) over the loaded face(s): face 14 carries (100.052, 0.000, 0.000) N.
For reference, the source solved this with second-order tetrahedra (Netgen, maximum element size 2 mm).

Outputs:
- max_displacement_mm [mm]: maximum nodal displacement magnitude in the part

Submit results.json containing exactly an outputs object with these numeric keys. Also submit main.py, part.step, mesh.msh, fields.npz, solver.log, refinement.json and environment.json. See candidate README for the artifact contract. Correct numerical answers alone do not establish workflow completion.

outputs.definition: maximum nodal displacement magnitude in the part
